papers.title: The dual role of Rpt3 in protecting cells from proteotoxic damage.
papers.summary: Rpt3, a proteasome base subunit, protects cells against proteotoxic stress in yeast and human cells. Overexpression reduced ER-stress sensitivity in ire1Δ/hac1Δ mutants, enhanced proteasome assembly and activity, and raised Hac1 levels. Its rescue depended on Rpn4 and ubiquitinating enzymes/chaperones, revealing a dual role: boosting proteasomal activity while upregulating Hac1 to maintain proteostasis.

papers.title: MAD2B guides chromosome stability in mitosis via the MAD2B-CIP2A signaling axis.
papers.summary: MAD2B safeguards genome integrity during mitosis via a newly identified interaction with CIP2A, mediated by CIP2A's N-terminus. MAD2B depletion triggered DNA damage response and replication stress, causing aberrant mitotic DNA synthesis, and disrupted CIP2A recruitment to γH2AX-marked lesions. The MAD2B-CIP2A axis links replication-stress surveillance to mitotic chromosome repair.

papers.title: Jer1-Ga2-LpR1 axis mediates upstream input of alpha-mannosidosis.
papers.summary: This paper establishes the first Drosophila model of alpha-mannosidosis (AMD) and identifies three novel upstream factors—Jer1, Ga2, LpR1—acting through a Jer1–Ga2–LpR1 axis. Jer1 recruits E3 ligase Ga2 to ubiquitinate LpR1 for lysosomal degradation; knockdown reduces lysosomal burden and rescues lethal phenotype. Mammalian counterparts IPP, UBE3C, VLDLR are functionally conserved, suggesting therapeutic targets.

papers.title: B Cell Mechanisms Underlie IgG Glycan Alterations in Obesity.
papers.summary: Studying pediatric obesity, the authors show IgG is hyposialylated and hypogalactosylated (most prominent in females), linked to B-cell upregulation of Wnt3, a GWAS-identified glycosylation candidate. Wnt3's role was confirmed in HEK293FS and ARH-77 cell models. Obesity thus drives IgG hyposialylation through previously unrecognized Wnt3 actions regulating IgG galactosylation in B cells, offering potential insulin-resistance targets.

papers.title: The transcription factor CLAMP is required for neurogenesis in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: CLAMP, a Drosophila transcription factor, is required for neural stem cell (NSC) stemness, proliferation, and optic-lobe development. A null mutant shows it promotes stemness/proliferation/glial genes and represses neurogenesis genes. CLAMP directly binds master regulators Notch and Tailless, providing a mechanistic link to severe optic-lobe deficits. CLAMP coordinates a core transcriptional program driving NSC proliferation and differentiation.

papers.title: Starve-Feed Cycles Direct Quiescence to Proliferation Transitions in Drosophila Follicle Stem Cells via Transcriptional Regulation.
papers.summary: Using TU-tagging in Drosophila follicle stem cells, the authors probed quiescence-to-proliferation (Q-P) transitions driven by feeding. Unexpectedly, cell-cycle regulators were not induced. A sequential screen uncovered seven novel feeding-dependent Q-P regulators, including a cholesterol transporter and glial/neuronal genes, underscoring dynamic gene-expression control in how stem cells translate dietary signals into proliferation decisions.

papers.title: Schisandra chinensis polysaccharide attenuates diabetic islet cell injury by promoting autophagy via suppression of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade.
papers.summary: Schisandra chinensis polysaccharide (SCP) alleviated diabetes in rats and β-TC-6 cells by promoting protective autophagy via inhibition of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR cascade. SCP dose-dependently reduced hyperglycemia and weight loss, improved β-cell function and islet histology; high-dose efficacy was comparable to metformin. Chloroquine co-treatment abolished the effects, confirming autophagy dependence.

papers.title: TET1-mediated DNA demethylation and transcription activation of MRPS17 induces lung adenocarcinoma through PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway.
papers.summary: MRPS17 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and correlates with poor prognosis. Overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and invasion; knockdown induced apoptosis and reduced tumorigenicity. TET1 demethylates the MRPS17 promoter, enhancing expression and activating PI3K-AKT-mTOR. The TET1-MRPS17 axis is a novel epigenetic mechanism, positioning MRPS17 as a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.title: miR-142-3p in cancer: intracellular tumor suppression and extracellular vesicle- mediated microenvironmental signaling.
papers.summary: A review of miR-142-3p in cancer, which acts tumor-suppressively intracellularly (inhibiting proliferation/EMT, promoting apoptosis and chemosensitivity) while being selectively exported in extracellular vesicles to exert context-dependent microenvironmental roles—regulating CAF activation, angiogenesis, immunity, and possibly cachexia. Discusses therapeutic strategies to restore intracellular miR-142-3p or modulate its EV-mediated transfer.

papers.title: Disruption of cellular timekeeping in cancer: links between circadian clocks, metabolism, and tumor progression.
papers.summary: This review links circadian clock disruption to cancer via metabolic reprogramming. Clock genes (CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, CRY) regulate cell cycle, metabolism, DNA repair, and apoptosis; their dysfunction promotes glycolysis, lipid production, genetic instability, and metastasis. The authors highlight chronotherapy—timing treatment to biological rhythms—as a path to improve efficacy and reduce toxicity, advancing chronobiology-informed precision oncology.

papers.title: Preliminary miRNA profiling of plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants.
papers.summary: Plasma miRNA profiling identified 65 miRNAs differentially expressed in both Delta and Omicron SARS-CoV-2 infections versus healthy controls, with associations to symptom severity and outcomes. Across Delta phases, 38 miRNAs changed. mRNA-miRNA interaction analysis highlighted PTEN, IGF1R, MYC, and STAT3. Provides insight into host epigenetic responses to distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy.

papers.title: Advances in ferroptosis and cuproptosis: implications for spinal cord injury.
papers.summary: A review of ferroptosis and cuproptosis in spinal cord injury (SCI), where blood-spinal cord barrier disruption floods the injury site with copper and iron ions, triggering both cell-death pathways. Covers mechanisms, key genes, signaling, co-regulatory networks, and targeted pathway therapies, proposing dual regulation of cuproptosis and ferroptosis as an innovative treatment strategy for SCI.

papers.title: Low-molecular-weight components of placental extract inhibit degranulation by blocking Ca(2+) influx in rat basophilic leukemia cells.
papers.summary: Low-molecular-weight (approximately 200-400 Da) components of porcine placental extract (PPE) inhibited degranulation in RBL-2H3 mast cells dose-dependently by blocking extracellular Ca2+ influx rather than intracellular Ca2+ release. PPE did not affect Syk phosphorylation but inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Findings point to low-MW PPE components as leads for novel antiallergic drugs.

papers.title: Identification of ZmGLN5, a candidate gene for resistance to Gibberella ear rot in maize.
papers.summary: Comparative transcriptomics in maize lines contrasting for Gibberella ear rot (GER) resistance identified defense-related pathways and nine candidate genes. ZmGLN5, encoding glutamine synthetase 5, was validated by gene-based association and mutagenesis; an indel marker based on its first-intron variation was validated in 150 inbred lines. ZmGLN5 is a key candidate for improving GER resistance in maize breeding.

papers.title: Therapeutic effects of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D(3) with astragalus polysaccharide on insulin resistance in gestational diabetes mellitus rat models.
papers.summary: Combined 1,25(OH)2D3 and astragalus polysaccharide (APS) alleviated insulin resistance and metabolic disorders in gestational diabetes rat models. The combination lowered serum glucose and lipids, reduced hepatic ROS/MDA, raised SOD, upregulated VDR and insulin signaling (IRS1, GLUT2, PI3K/AKT), suppressed FOXO1/gluconeogenesis/lipogenesis, and showed VDR–PI3K p85 interaction, supporting VDR upregulation plus oxidative-stress attenuation as the mechanism.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of novel alternatively spliced isoforms of the human RAB8B gene.
papers.summary: Two novel alternatively spliced isoforms of human RAB8B were identified by combining in silico analysis with RT-PCR, semi-nested PCR, and DNA sequencing. Predicted protein products differ from canonical RAB8B in length and physicochemical properties; structural modeling and molecular dynamics indicate isoform-specific stability/flexibility differences, notably between active and inactive states. Expands the RAB8B transcript repertoire as a foundation for functional studies.

papers.title: PIK3CA silencing restores anoikis sensitivity in endothelial cells.
papers.summary: PIK3CA (p110α) silencing in anoikis-resistant endothelial cells reversed malignancy-associated traits—restoring anoikis sensitivity and wild-type-like morphology, clonogenicity, proliferation, invasion, and adhesion. It increased apoptosis with altered pro-/anti-apoptotic molecule expression and enhanced caspase activation. Demonstrates that PIK3CA silencing reverses key features of the anoikis-resistant phenotype, revealing mechanisms of anoikis resistance.

papers.title: Association of EBV EBNA1 C-terminal variations with severity of Invasive ductal carcinoma.
papers.summary: Examining EBV EBNA1 C-terminal variants in 30 EBV-positive breast cancer biopsies, the predominant p-Thr prototype (70%) and co-infection with v-Leu (30%) were seen mostly in higher-grade invasive ductal carcinoma, but no significant association with severity was found. Fifteen consensus SNPs and six random mutations, plus phylogenetic similarity to reference NC_009334, were reported. No association between EBNA1 variation and breast cancer severity.

papers.title: PINK1-Parkin pathway-mediated mitophagy in sepsis: friend or foe?
papers.summary: A review of PINK1-Parkin-mediated mitophagy in sepsis, proposing four interacting mechanistic pathways—oxidative stress, cGAS-STING, NF-κB signaling, and inflammasome activation—that contribute to sepsis pathogenesis. Explores candidate agents (PINK1 activators, Parkin recruiters, deubiquitinase inhibitors, upstream modulators) to regulate mitophagy with protective potential against septic multi-organ injury including encephalopathy, cardiac dysfunction, lung, and kidney injury.

papers.title: NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome is associated with formaldehyde-induced reproductive and metabolic dysfunction: protective role of quercetin in rats.
papers.summary: In male rats, subchronic formaldehyde exposure induced metabolic dysfunction, testicular damage, and oxidative stress via DAMPs-driven NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome activation (TNF-α/TLR4) while repressing steroidogenesis. Quercetin co-treatment dose-dependently ameliorated these effects, with 100 mg/kg most effective; molecular docking suggested quercetin binds TNF, TLR4, NF-κB, and NLRP3 more strongly. Supports quercetin as a nutraceutical against environmental aldehyde toxicity.

papers.title: Mitogenomic Architecture and Phylogenetic Insights Shed Light on the Matrilineal Evolution of the Mahseer Fish Neolissochilus sumatranus (Cyprinidae: Torinae) in Southeast Asia.
papers.summary: NGS-assembled mitogenome of Neolissochilus sumatranus (16,584 bp; 37 genes plus control region) showed conserved organization versus nine congeners, purifying selection on most protein-coding genes, canonical cloverleaf tRNAs, and conserved control-region sequence blocks. Phylogenetics support Torinae monophyly and close N. sumatranus–N. hendersoni–N. soroides relatedness (Sundaland); clarifies the species' position within Torinae for systematics and management.
